faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium cardiovascular stent?
faq.a: Nitinol (Ni-Ti shape memory alloy) provides the unique superelasticity required for self-expanding stents and TAVI frames. The alloy undergoes martensitic transformation at body temperature.

faq.q: How is a titanium cardiovascular stent manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium cardiovascular stent is manufactured using Laser micro-cutting; Shape-setting heat treatment; Electropolishing. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Nitinol (ASTM F2063) for titanium cardiovascular stent?
What standards apply to titanium cardiovascular stent?
faq.a: Titanium Cardiovascular Stent components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium cardiovascular stent?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Austenite finish temperature (Af) must be tuned to 25+-3C for self-expanding behavior at body temperature; Surface defects >5um after electropolishing can cause fatigue crack initiation. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium cardiovascular stent?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
